text:
maria: Quick design check — I'm trying a different way to group items in the left shelf to cut visual noise. Sketch: https://img.redwood/mock/side-shelf-v2.png. Proposal: collapse 'Models' + 'Serving' + 'Runtimes' into a single 'Inference' shelf with an optional sub-nav. Thoughts on deep links and breadcrumbs if we do this? :thinking:

dan: :eyes: I like the idea of fewer high-level entries. Two quick questions: (1) what happens to existing permalinks users may have bookmarked? (2) how will the breadcrumb read — e.g. Inference > Model > Versions or just Model > Versions?

maria: Good call. For permalinks we want stable slugs. Plan A: keep old routes as redirects to new path (server-side) and maintain a compatibility mapping for 6 months. Breadcrumb example I'm leaning to: Inference / Models / model-name / version-id. That keeps the top-level shelf visible.

olivia: Accessibility nits: if we group more, keyboard users should still be able to skip to the active subsection quickly. Need a visible focus ring on the shelf header and ensure aria-current on the active leaf link. Also check screenreader order — nesting should be announced logically.

kevin: Agree with Olivia. One more thing: deep links that land on a nested view (e.g., /models/:id/metrics) need to expand the parent shelf and set appropriate aria-expanded. Otherwise users think nothing happened.

sam: routing note — here's a rough router contract to keep us consistent:```js
// example route mapping
{
  "/inference/models": "Inference > Models",
  "/inference/models/:id": "Inference > Models > :id",
  "/inference/deployments/:id": "Inference > Deployments > :id"
}
// old routes redirect:
"/models/:id" -> "/inference/models/:id"
```

maria: Nice. Does anyone have concerns about mobile/compact width? The shelf collapses into a single icon bar — will deep links still open the right pane? We should guarantee a landing behavior.

navin: Mobile yes — deep links should expand the shelf programmatically on load. Edge case: if user has a persistent collapse preference, deep link should override once so they land in the content, but not change their saved preference. 

olivia: Also flag for QA: verify focus landing after deep link. Focus should move to the first actionable element in the main column (h1 or primary CTA) after navigation, not remain on the shelf.

kevin: Copy/SEO note: breadcrumb separators — we should use visually a chevron but announce as "slash" or "greater than"? ARIA breadcrumb spec says list structure — let's keep it semantically a nav > ol > li. Screenreaders will handle it.

maria: Quick poll — prefer "Inference" as shelf label or something friendlier like "Runtime" or "Serving"? :poll:

dan: "Serving" feels ambiguous to non-engineers. "Inference" is technical but accurate. 

sam: +1 Inference. Less chance of mismatch with other product terms.

olivia: +1 for clarity. Also propose a tooltip with short copy: "Models, deployments, and runtimes for serving your models" for discovery.

maria: Ok going to run a short hallway test tomorrow. Can someone from eng confirm routing/backwards-compat redirect plan? @dan?

dan: I'll put up a short spec in eng-platform today. Will include redirect mapping and a feature flag so we can flip back. Also will add analytics for broken permalinks.

navin: One more edge: query params used for A/B (e.g., ?eval=123) should be preserved through redirects. We don't want those dropped.

maria: Great call. Adding to the spec. If folks are good with this, I'll update the mock and the component library tokens.

deploy-bot: Preview of the shelf prototype is up: https://deploy.redwood/pr/1423 (shelf-v2). Screenshot and keyboard walkthrough included. :rocket:

kevin: Checked the preview — anchor links to sections work but I noticed the URL changes to include a hash (/#deployments) and the breadcrumb doesn't update. That should be dynamic and reflect true route state, not only hash.

sam: That is a bug — will fix router to replace history state instead of only toggling fragment. Thanks for catching.

maria: Thanks everyone — will merge design updates once Dan's redirect spec is in and Sam's router tweak is scheduled. Leaving a few TODOs in the thread for QA and copy. :thumbsup:
